result.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
result.summary: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Pitfall Anticipation World Model（PAWM），让 world model 不逐步预测下一观测，而是在有界多步未来内预判即将发生的失败（pitfall）并仅在潜在风险出现时选择性介入，用合成数据 SFT 加与黑盒 LLM 的 GRPO 协同训练，在 ScienceWorld 与 WebArena-Lite 上提升黑盒 agent 表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测什么」与「何时调用 foresight」的取舍，以及抽象失败信号而非逐步观测的监督方式，可供核查 LVR 中何时引入视觉证据、以及用任务相关结果而非细粒度状态做预测监督的线索；但为纯文本 agent 设定，无可迁移的视觉内部状态证据。
